proposal.summary: SH-CS initially asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing-dispute tickets and auto-fix "wrong bills" (CL-01), framing the August-September dispute volume doubling (E-04) as a response-speed/generic-defect problem. Investigation showed CS response times were within SLA (E-03), so that framing was rejected; a later-invalidated first problem (PD-1@v1, bill-shock) was replaced by PD-1@v2, which established that 1,184 of the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills had valid pre-cutoff AMI reads wrongly rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12), caused by rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling, E-13) comparing raw register values from firmware v4.2 meters (which report in 0.1 m3, E-14) against m3-based 12-month history. This confirmed mechanism explains only the ESTIMATED-read subset of disputes, not the larger 1,785-record ACTUAL-read-dominant share (E-01). The release ships only two low-risk deliverables — dispute ticket response templates explaining the confirmed mechanism and dispute-volume trend monitoring — while the rule fix, rebill-candidate identification, and rule-ownership escalation remain blocked and are documented as known limitations rather than silently dropped.
key_points: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1,180-1,260/month (Aug-Sep) and stayed elevated (E-04), the trigger for the investigation.
Of 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, 1,184 had a valid pre-cutoff AMI read that was nonetheless rejected on billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12).

Root mechanism identified: rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13), while firmware v4.2 meters (rollout June 2026) report values in 0.1 m3 units (E-14), misclassifying legitimate reads as high consumption.

The confirmed mechanism accounts only for the ESTIMATED-read subset of disputes; it does not explain the larger ACTUAL-read-dominant share (1,785 of E-01), which remains an open question (VOB-U-CONSUMPTION-DRIVER).

Alternative explanations were tested and rejected with evidence: tariff change (E-02, ruled out), CS response-time bottleneck (E-03, within SLA), field manual-read backlog as dominant cause (contradicted by E-01/E-10/E-12), and AMI handoff failure (contradicted by E-01/E-12).
DEFINE Gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs); the Release Gate decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no items on hold.
Released scope: draft_ticket_response_templates:DA-TICKET and monitor_dispute_volume_trend:DA-TICKET, consistent with the no-automated-bill-write constraint (K-BILLWRITE, SC-NOWRITE).
No write_bill_adjustment actions were taken by the agent; any actual bill correction requires separate SH-BILL-authorized action under K-BILLWRITE.
limitations_explained: Three verification obligations remain OPEN and are explicitly outside this release's scope: the driver behind the ACTUAL-read-dominant disputes (VOB-U-CONSUMPTION-DRIVER), the rebill-candidate population and adjustment amounts for the 1,184 affected accounts (VOB-U-REBILL-POPULATION), and who owns deploying the BV-17 fix (VOB-U-RULE-FIX-OWNER).

The BV-17 rule defect itself was identified but not fixed: billing-config is read-only to this agent, so correcting the unit-scaling bug (SR-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING) was not feasible within the remaining contest time.

The confirmed BV-17/firmware v4.2 mechanism only explains the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills; the cause of the larger 1,785-record ACTUAL-read-dominant share of disputes (E-01) is still unconfirmed.

query_consumption_trend_by_account:DA-BILL, identify_rebill_candidate_accounts:DA-BILL, and escalate_billing_rule_defect:DA-RULES were all planned in-scope actions that could not ship because their blocking VOBs remain open.

Even once a technical fix exists, actually correcting bills for the 1,184 affected accounts requires separate action by SH-BILL under the K-BILLWRITE authority constraint; this agent's scope only ever covered identification, not writing adjustments, and that identification step itself is undelivered.

The DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, not a full pass, meaning deferred critical unknowns (e.g., handoff H-MDMS-BILL delivery/semantic validity unknown) were tracked as obligations rather than resolved before scoping the release.
